    <item>
      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/global-development">Global development</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/senegal">Senegal</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/lgbt-rights">LGBTQ+ rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/anti-rights-movement">Anti-rights movement</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/africa">Africa</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/world">World news</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/law">Law</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/society/aids-and-hiv">Aids and HIV</category>
      <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:00:25 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5d08247e565b832f183d37b676fe7def25b19c25/213_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=123bd8ecc615f6c5a01371cef3492c23">

        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Jane Hahn/AP</media:credit>
      </media:content>
      <media:content width="700" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5d08247e565b832f183d37b676fe7def25b19c25/213_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=700&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=80b82662e7e790a0db106b737b3aa2cb">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Jane Hahn/AP</media:credit>
      </media:content>

      <title>Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize</link>
      <description><p>Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</p><p></p><p>The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/israel-committed-genocide-in-gaza-says-un-inquiry">that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</a>.</p><p>The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:18:45 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Perspective</category><title>War escalates between Houthis and Riyadh: How did we get here?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261015-war-escalates-between-houthis-and-riyadh-how-did-we-get-here</link><description>
To discuss the ongoing conflict between the Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed coalition, we speak to Jules Grange Gastinel, a researcher at France's CNRS research body specialising in the Houthi movement. He tells us why the conflict has escalated and what the Houthis want.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dee9186e-c89f-11f1-9be4-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a8242456.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dee9186e-c89f-11f1-9be4-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a8242456.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ed87506-c87c-11f1-98a8-af119fcfe771</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:16:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Oliver FARRY</dc:creator></item><item><category><![CDATA[People & Profit]]></category><title>French crypto unicorn Ledger warns of AI security risks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/people-profit/20261015-french-crypto-unicorn-ledger-warns-of-ai-security-risks</link><description>
Artificial intelligence is "changing the security landscape". That's according to Ledger, a French unicorn of cryptocurrency that's seeking a bigger role in digital security. Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet says: "Finding vulnerabilities and exploiting them costs almost nothing. So this is the new challenge that we have, as the security industry in general – how can we raise the bar for security so it becomes so difficult to break systems? And I think hardware is part of the equation."
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bdefecae-c891-11f1-863e-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/People-Profit-LEDGER-15-OCT-more.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/bdefecae-c891-11f1-863e-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/People-Profit-LEDGER-15-OCT-more.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">92ff141c-c881-11f1-b690-cb2e7d1cc6a3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:31:22 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Kate MOODY</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>‘Amazing progress’ in lung cancer: Immunotherapy extends survival as mRNA vaccines offer hope</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261015-amazing-progress-in-lung-cancer-immunotherapy-extends-survival-as-mrna-vaccines-offer-hope</link><description>
François Picard is pleased to welcome Siow-Ming Lee, Professor of Medical Oncology at the University College London and a specialist in lung cancer. “Lung cancer is not one cancer. There are many different types of lung cancer,” explains Lee. For decades, lung cancer has been closely associated with smoking, late diagnosis and poor survival prospects. Yet there is a broader revolution in cancer brewing: Medicine advances in molecular oncology, minimally invasive surgery and immunotherapy are fundamentally transforming both the understanding and treatment of the disease, including among patients who have never smoked.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a0cc41e-c89a-11f1-a284-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bf305ca9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a0cc41e-c89a-11f1-a284-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bf305ca9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6912440c-c89b-11f1-891a-dd239350d4ee</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:22:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>François PICARD</dc:creator></item><item><category>arts24</category><title>From Lupin's return to a bloody culinary apocalypse: The TV shows to watch this month</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/arts24/20261015-from-lupin-s-return-to-a-bloody-culinary-apocalypse-the-tv-shows-to-watch-this-month</link><description>
TV critic Dheepthika Laurent takes us through this month's TV highlights, starting with the long-awaited return of "Lupin", Netflix's most-watched French series. Omar Sy is back as the gentleman thief, but this time someone appears to be stealing in his name. Can France's favourite master of disguise clear his name?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/57f34236-c885-11f1-86e7-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-c2f6f3c5.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/57f34236-c885-11f1-86e7-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-c2f6f3c5.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3de8e9ae-c885-11f1-8de2-45cb51ca235a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:08:26 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Eve JACKSON</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Elon Musk and Donald Trump: What their growing ties mean for Ukraine</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261015-elon-musk-and-donald-trump-what-their-growing-ties-mean-for-ukraine</link><description>
The recent disruption of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine comes as Washington steps up pressure on Kyiv to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries. The system plays a key role in Ukraine’s long-range drone operations, raising questions about the implications of the disruption and Elon Musk’s increasingly close ties with Donald Trump.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9579dc0a-c894-11f1-a670-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-140816-140948-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9579dc0a-c894-11f1-a670-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-140816-140948-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9a36d00e-c894-11f1-a3e5-c3f8d9655db0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 12:39:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Windblown yardangs on Mars | Space photo of the day for Oct. 15, 2026 ]]>

A new image from the European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft reveals the powerful erosive forces that have shaped and re-shaped the surface of the Red Planet over long periods of geological time.

What is it?

This new Mars Express image captures Amazonis Mensa, a large, flat mountain on the Red Planet that offers planetary scientists a glimpse into the many factors that can sculpt a world's surface.

In this photograph, several features stand out to help illustrate this. Easiest to make out are the large round craters created by ancient impacts on the surface of Mars. However, many of these craters have been at least partially filled by lava flowing across the surface of the Red Planet around three billion years ago, according a statement from the European Space Agency (ESA) accompanying the image.

More interestingly, rippled structures known as yardangs can be seen to the left and right sides of the image. These ridges "form as loose sand particles are whipped up by wind and deployed a little like a cosmic sandblaster," according to ESA.

In the image, the two groups of yardangs ripple across the Martian surface in two different directions. This is because Amazonis Mensa acts as a windbreak, pushing material blown by winds in separate orientations.

Why is it incredible?

For over 20 years, Mars Express has been providing scientists with an unparalleled look at the Martian surface, helping us better understand the forces that have shaped the Red Planet over eons.

]]> <![CDATA[ Beat light pollution with these six portable telescopes ]]> Light pollution is the astronomer's biggest enemy, especially if you're gazing into deep space. And while some of the best telescopes can make a difference, there's no way to eliminate it. That's why, if you want to observe the cosmos without obstruction, you need to seek out darker skies, get a smart telescope or combine the two.

You don't have to book a flight to a dark sky reserve; just traveling away from suburbia can be enough. That's where portable telescopes come in. Set one up in a field, for example, and you'll get a vastly improved view of the cosmos. Galaxies, nebulas and other deep space objects become more detailed when they're not washed out by skyglow.

We've picked out six telescopes you can take on the road: Some, such as the DwarfLab Dwarf Mini, are small enough you could even put them in a backpack and hop on your bicycle.

All but one are smart telescopes, meaning that when you do get to your desired location, you can pick from a list of stellar sights to home in on. And while they may be portable, they're powerful with it.

So, beat light pollution and say hello to stunning views of the night sky.

]]> <![CDATA[ Scientists discover 'chemical starter kit' for life in planetary birthplaces ]]> Methanol, coming as part of the 'chemical starter kit' around young stars, has produced some unexpected surprises that could ultimately reveal some of the conditions in which planets and potentially life form around protostars.

The methanol discoveries were made by astronomers using ALMA (the Atacama Large millimeter/submillimeter Array) in the Atacama Desert in Chile, as part of a project called COMPASS (the Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys).

"Our work provides insight into the complex chemistry of young star systems and is ultimately an important piece of the puzzle in understanding the origin of life," said University of Bern astrophysicist Maria Drozdovskaya, who leads the COMPASS project, in a statement.

Drozdovskaya's multinational team of more than 30 astronomers has been chasing down complex organic molecules, large molecules that include carbon atoms, in the planetary construction yards around eleven young stars.

These molecules form part of the chemical inventory that ultimately builds planets and, perhaps, even life that will one day live on those planets.

Methanol matters

Methanol (CH3OH) is important because it is highly abundant in star- and planet-forming regions. In fact, it’s the most abundant complex organic molecule to be found in interstellar space, and is commonly found in planet-forming disks.

Its sheer abundance means that, of all the molecules found around young stars, methanol is the easiest in which to detect different forms where regular hydrogen atoms are replaced by a heavier isotope of hydrogen called deuterium.

How many molecules contain these heavier isotopes is highly dependent upon the conditions in which planets are forming within the disk.

That’s why the COMPASS team used ALMA to search for these forms of methanol in the gas belonging to the planet-forming disks around the 11 nearby low-mass protostars. The observations have also helped assess the general chemical diversity of these disks.

The unexpected discovery of a methanol molecule containing deuterium was made in the planet-forming disk around only one of those 11 stars, namely the young star IRAS 4A2, located about a thousand light-years away in the Perseus Molecular Cloud.

IRAS refers to the Infrared Astronomical Satellite, which was a joint NASA–UK–Netherlands mission launched in 1983 and which first detected this young star as a source of infrared light through the thick gas and dust of the molecular cloud.

The COMPASS team also discovered methanol maser emission from more than half of the 11 protostars, favoring the youngest of the stars. A maser is a microwave version of a laser in the sense that the microwave emission is being stimulated and then amplified, but astrophysical masers occur naturally, often in shock fronts as methanol molecules collide and are excited.

Methanol masers have previously been detected in planet-forming disks around turbulent high-mass protostars, but COMPASS’ observations are the first detection of them around calmer lower-mass protostars.

"The fact that it has now also been found in a low-mass protostar shows that locally extreme physical conditions can prevail there analogously to massive stars and challenges our previous understanding of the formation of sun-like stars," said Drozdovskaya.

The finding implies that methanol masers are a common product of all planet-forming discs and therefore are produced by processes that are universal in star- and planet-birth, regardless of the protostar's mass.

For example, thermal bursts from the growing star as it accumulates gas from its surroundings could generate shocks in a planet-forming disk, stimulating maser activity in the abundant methanol.

"Both results underscore how important high-performance spectroscopic measurements like those from COMPASS with ALMA are for detecting rare and previously unknown chemical phenomena," said Drozdovskaya, referring to both the methanol masers and the deuterium-rich methanol molecules around IRAS 4A2. "They show just how much we still have to learn about the chemical processes in young protostellar systems."

The new findings have at least begun to answer some questions, such as how the diversity in this 'chemical starter kit' varies from star to star, with ALMA detecting some subtle differences, such as variations in the abundance of oxygen- and nitrogen-bearing molecular species among the eleven stars.

However, questions about how the chemistry of young star systems arises and how it influences the evolution of those systems remain unanswered.

For now, the COMPASS team is painstakingly and systematically studying the data on all the different types of molecules detected in their ALMA observations, and preparing follow-up studies with other facilities including the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

"The analysis of all the collected data will take several more years," said Drozdovskaya.

The first results from COMPASS are published in seven papers [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] in the October 2026 issue of the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX wants to launch Starship more than 450 times per year from South Texas ]]> SpaceX wants to start flying its Starship megarocket a lot more often.

The company has requested permission to launch Starship from its Starbase site in South Texas up to 456 times per year. That's a big jump from the currently allowed cadence of 25.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is in the early stages of reviewing the request. Today (Oct. 14), the agency announced "its intent to prepare a Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, open a public scoping period and hold public scoping meetings for SpaceX’s proposal."

Starship, which stands more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall, is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. It's also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX believes will revolutionize spaceflight.

The megarocket has flown 14 times to date, all of them test flights from Starbase, which is near the Texas border city of Brownsville. On the most recent jaunt, which lifted off on Sept. 28, Starship reached orbit for the first time and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites — the first members of a new broadband constellation that could eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft.

Assembling that network will require a lot of Starship launches. And even more will be needed to build SpaceX's planned Starmind AI megaconstellation, which Elon Musk has said will harbor a million satellites. Indeed, the world's richest man has said that SpaceX is targeting more than 10,000 Starship liftoffs per year by 2030.

Not all of those flights will originate from Starbase, which hosts two orbital pads. SpaceX is working to get three Starship pads up and running on Florida's Space Coast, and the company aims to break ground on a $100 billion, 12-pad complex in Louisiana next year.

Each operational Starship launch will also feature two landings. Both of the vehicle's elements — the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — are designed to return to the pad after liftoff, where they will be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. So SpaceX's proposal for 456 launches from Starbase per year includes a request for approval for 912 landings.

SpaceX plans to work up to this cadence in two phases, according to the FAA. Phase 1 "would include up to 100 annual launches and up to 200 annual landings (100 of Starship and 100 of Super Heavy)," the agency wrote. "Launches and landings could occur any day or time of the week."

Crew-12 astronauts will address the media this afternoon (Oct. 15) to discuss their mission and their return after nearly eight months on orbit. A live broadcast of that event will also be available to stream on Space.com's homepage beginning at 3:30 p.m. EDT (1930 GMT).

Cargo Dragon's nominal orbital insertion on Tuesday placed it on course to catch up with the ISS after a 51-hour LEO chase. After rendezvous this morning, Dragon will autonomously dock to the zenith port on the station's Harmony module. ]]> <![CDATA[ Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 'families,' scientists find ]]> You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.

The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way.

The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets, that are potentially capable of hosting life. That could be crucial as astronomers search for life beyond the solar system, pointing them to systems with potentially habitable planets like Earth.

"The fundamental question we started from was: What determines the characteristics of planetary systems as we see them today? Are they established at birth or sculpted by evolution over time? The truth, in the end, turned out to lie somewhere in the middle," team member and INAF researcher Diego Turrini said in a statement sent to Space.com.

"Our results show that there is a genetic link between planetary systems and their stars, and that, depending on the star around which they are born, this link also determines their fate," Turrini added.

What is the genetic code of a planetary system?

The first "family" the scientists identified consists of wide, massive systems, often with total masses between two and 10 times that of our own solar system. The planets in these systems orbit stars more massive than the sun with lower concentrations of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium (which astronomers somewhat confusingly call metals) than seen in our star.

The second family is more compact and lower-mass systems. The members of this family are composed of planets with comparable masses and sizes, a so-called "peas-in-a-pod" configuration. They orbit stars with mass and metallicity equal to or lower than those of the sun, with orbits that are usually much tighter than those of Mercury, the closest planet to the sun.

One of the "genes" Turrini and colleagues selected to sort planetary systems into families was the deviations that planets make from orbiting their star in the same circular plane. That, in turn, reveals a family history of violent gravitational instability caused by events like giant collisions and planetary ejections.

Violent events were common for the first family, but much less so for the second group of planetary systems, the researchers found. They determined that the number of these turbulent events a planetary system experiences can be linked to even modest variations in the environment in which planets form. These variations arise due to different properties of the parent star of those systems.

Thus, the nature of the star in these systems doesn't just fundamentally change the formation of planets in their systems; it influences the system's future evolution, determining whether it will be characterized by phases of marked instability and giant impacts.

"The main difficulty during the data analysis was determining whether the two families of planetary systems were real or just an illusion created by the technological limits of current observational techniques," said team member Camilla Danielski, of the University of Valencia in Spain.

"At the end of the path, it became clear that selection effects acted as the tip of the iceberg, revealing the existence of much deeper structural diversities between these systems," Danielski said.

The scientists tested their conclusions by running simulations of planetary system evolution, all of which began with different conditions.

"The scenarios that best reproduce the dynamical properties of the family of wide and massive systems are those in which the systems are unstable from birth," said research supervisor and INAF researcher Danae Polychroni. "The greater abundance of material from which planets form around their host stars causes them to be born too large, preventing the system from remaining stable."

The team's research was published on Tuesday (Oct. 13) in the journal Nature Astronomy.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' author Matt Dinniman talks inspirations, success, and the upcoming Peacock TV series (interview) ]]> Fall has officially arrived, and as autumn leaves blaze in vivid colors, there is no better time to plunge into the imaginative world of New York Times best-selling author Matt Dinniman's "Dungeon Crawler Carl", the wildly addictive science fantasy book series that's taking the world by storm.

Even if you haven't read them, you've probably seen folks carrying these books, emblazoned with their loud, neon-colored covers, at your neighborhood coffee house. You'll see it even more in the future, too, as a streaming adaptation of the novels is coming to Peacock, with Seth MacFarlane's Fuzzy Door and co-showrunners Eric Heisserer and Chris Yost at the helm.

The eighth book in the series, "A Parade of Horribles," dropped in May of 2026 and continues the story of Carl and his ex-girlfriend’s precocious pussy cat named Princess Donut as they try to navigate the dangerously daunting levels of a lethal doomsday dungeon for an intergalactic television show deciding the fate of humanity and the planet Earth.

Think Douglas Adams's "The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy" meets "The Running Man" and "Ready Player One" in the "Dungeons & Dragons" RPG realm, and you've got a pretty good idea of the stylistic narrative you'll soon discover when you dare to enter Dinniman's slightly demented literary world.

"The genesis is that I’ve been writing my whole life, and I have a thousand story ideas," Dinniman tells Space on the origins of his sci-fi sensation. "I’ve kept a running list of ideas since childhood, and this one had been on there for some time. The line in my list for this particular one was 'Alien' game show.'"

With over 14 million copies of the "Dungeon Crawler Carl" series sold to date, spooky season is the ideal jumping-on moment so you can share your favorite sadistic dungeon level kill next time you're at a cool cocktail party or fun family function!

"The success is a whole other question. I think I just happened to hit the right story at the right time," admits Dinniman. "It's about a man pushing back against impossible odds. The antagonist isn't just a single person or entity, but an entire system designed to crush any life out of him, all for the entertainment of the masses. That sort of story seems to really be resonating right now. Plus there's a talking cat in it."

Dinniman has described the most recently-released sequel as "the Carl and Donut version of Mariokart—only deadlier," with the cruel dungeon architects tightening their brutal grip. As the current king of LitRPG titles in circulation, "Dungeon Crawler Carl" is the next best thing to a living video game.

"Luckily I’m still in love with this story, and I am in love with writing it," he admits. "It hasn’t gotten old yet. The end is in sight, and I’m more sad than anything that it'll eventually be over."

An episodic series adaptation seems like a no-brainer, and Peacock has wisely tapped into the considerable talents of both Heisserer ("Arrival," "Bird Box") and Yost ("Thor: The Dark World," "Thor: Ragnarok") for this ambitious TV project.

"Both Chris and Eric have a great amount of experience in Hollywood, but more importantly, both have read the books and like them," Dinniman notes. "Chris is a mega fan, and Eric knows more about gaming than any adult probably should. That's a great combination."

Dinniman also confirmed to us that he's serving as co-executive producer on the show, and will be involved throughout the production.

"The most important thing to preserve, I think, is the tone, which will also be the most challenging," states Dinniman. "Thankfully, the team that's been assembled is up to the challenge, and I can't wait for the world to see how it turns out."

With eight books released so far (and another two to come), you've got plenty of reading to do before the Peacock show and/or the next book lands. You can find the Dungeon Crawler Carl book series in your local bookstores and on Amazon. It's also available via Kindle e-readers and as an audiobook.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX's Starship just turned 10 years old. When will it go to Mars? ]]> Starship just reached orbit for the first time, carrying satellites for SpaceX's Starlink program. Analysts disagree on whether that's a detour or the destination — and what of the company's plans for the Red Planet?

Ten years ago, Elon Musk stood on stage at the International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Guadalajara, Mexico, and unveiled plans for a giant spaceship to carry people to Mars. This past Sept. 28 — a decade and a day later — the descendant of that vehicle reached orbit for the first time, on Starship's 14th-ever test flight.

The designs and hardware evolved greatly over those 10 years. For example, the 2016 design, called the Interplanetary Transport System (ITS), employed carbon fiber, but this gave way to the stainless-steel Starship, which SpaceX began testing in 2019 with short hops from its Texas site. Prototypes flew to high altitude and landed, and some exploded, until SN15 stuck a landing in May 2021. That same year, NASA selected Starship as the first astronaut lander for its Artemis lunar missions.

The full Starship stack — a Super Heavy booster with a Ship upper stage on top — first flew in April 2023 and failed within minutes. Three flights followed in less than a year, each reaching space, and each ending with Ship lost on reentry. During a 2024 test flight, SpaceX moved liquid oxygen between two tanks inside one Ship, the closest it has come to the propellant transfer that any mission to the moon or Mars will require. In June of that year, the company brought both stages down in controlled splashdowns, and that October the launch tower's mechanical arms caught a returning Super Heavy booster for the first time.

Progress wasn't linear, however. After a booster catch in January 2025, a string of Ship failures followed, and one upper stage exploded during ground testing that June. A clean flight in August 2025 helped break the streak, and by that October, SpaceX flew the last of the older design. The first Starship V3 launched in May 2026. Another went up in July, and Flight 14 followed on Sept. 28.

'A different beast'

"ITS was definitely a different beast," said Matija Renčelj of the European Space Policy Institute (ESPI). "Yet, we have to acknowledge two trends that both attest to SpaceX's agility and increasingly market-first rather than vision-first outlook."

"The gap between ITS and Starship is real, but I would not consider that a failure," he said.

In his view, the rocket is mainly a business tool. "The rocket is the means, not the end," Renčelj said, adding that its main role now is cutting Starlink deployment costs. SpaceX currently operates a constellation of more than 11,000 Starlink broadband satellites, almost all of which were launched by its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket. But Starship Flight 14 lofted the first members of the next-gen Starlink V3 constellation, which will eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft, if all goes to plan. Starlink V3 satellites are bigger and heavier than their predecessors and can only be launched efficiently by Starship.

Renčelj said the moon focus reflects Washington's priorities and SpaceX's interest in staying central to NASA's Artemis program, and in reassuring investors after the company's acquisition of xAI this past February and its IPO, which occurred in June.

Joseph Gonzalez, a University of Illinois Grainger College of Engineering aerospace professor who spent about a decade working on Artemis, sees it differently.

"I think SpaceX is still very much targeting Mars," he said. "SpaceX continues to stress making humanity multiplanetary and establishing a self-sufficient city on Mars as long-term objectives." Gonzalez sees the moon as a proving ground rather than a replacement. Just days away from Earth, the moon lets engineers find problems "before committing humans to a Mars mission."

"Space exploration takes time, especially when you are developing a human spaceflight system with this level of complexity," Gonzalez said. "They build, fly, learn, make changes and fly again. That creates very visible successes and failures, but it also allows engineers to accumulate flight experience and data quickly."

Challenges remain

Reaching Earth orbit isn't the hard part for Starship. Gonzalez said that the most underrated gap is the large-scale cryogenic propellant transfer between vehicles once in orbit. SpaceX has moved propellant between tanks in one Ship before, but its architecture requires numerous transfers involving tanker ships to refill a fuel depot, which a Ship must visit in order to make journeys to the moon or Mars. Gonzalez described this depot as a gas station in space, but there are challenges typical gas stations don't face. The fuel is extremely cold, for example, and it needs to be moved in microgravity conditions.

That milestone is yet to happen, and the timeline for an attempt is not clear. It could potentially come with Flight 15 and 16. These were aspirationally scheduled for no earlier than mid and late October, respectively, but have now apparently slipped to mid-to-late November (though there has been no public confirmation of any firm target date).

In 2025, Musk said there was a "50/50" chance of Starship making a run for Mars in 2026. However, with the once-every-26-months Mars launch window — which lasts a few weeks, opening in late October — and no propellant transfer demonstration yet in the books, that is off the table. The next such low-energy orbital transfer opportunity for the Red Planet opens in late 2028, running into early 2029. At the same time, NASA is currently targeting late 2028 for its Artemis IV mission — which involves Starship — to return humans to the lunar surface after an absence of more than 50 years, giving SpaceX a challenging deadline toward which to work. The company will need to dedicate key resources to meet that timeline, including developing life support systems for crew.

For now, Starship's most immediate role is hauling Starlink satellites in orbit. Renčelj noted that startups raising billions are betting on Starship delivering low super-launch prices along with Falcon 9-like reliability. "Their business models are underpinned by what might be a single point of failure," he said.

"Starship still has major capabilities to demonstrate before it can perform the complete missions envisioned for the moon and Mars," said Gonzalez.

"So I would say the timelines are comparable considering the ambition of the vehicles," he added. "The bigger difference isn't necessarily how many years they have taken, but it's where and how each program chooses to learn during those years."

Musk has repeatedly talked of getting thousands, or even hundreds of thousands, of people on Mars "to make life multiplanetary." Most immediately, SpaceX has a number of business goals and lunar commitments to adhere to ahead of a first uncrewed visit to Mars. Late 2028 appears to be the next real opportunity.

That same year, NASA selected Starship as the first astronaut lander for its Artemis lunar missions.

The full Starship stack — a Super Heavy booster with a Ship upper stage on top — first flew in April 2023 and failed within minutes. Three flights followed in less than a year, each reaching space, and each ending with Ship lost on reentry. During a 2024 test flight, SpaceX moved liquid oxygen between two tanks inside one Ship, the closest it has come to the propellant transfer that any mission to the moon or Mars will require. In June of that year, the company brought both stages down in controlled splashdowns, and that October the launch tower's mechanical arms caught a returning Super Heavy booster for the first time.

Progress wasn't linear, however. After a booster catch in January 2025, a string of Ship failures followed, and one upper stage exploded during ground testing that June. A clean flight in August 2025 helped break the streak, and by that October, SpaceX flew the last of the older design. The first Starship V3 launched in May 2026. Another went up in July, and Flight 14 followed on Sept. 28.

'A different beast'

"ITS was definitely a different beast," said Matija Renčelj of the European Space Policy Institute (ESPI). "Yet, we have to acknowledge two trends that both attest to SpaceX's agility and increasingly market-first rather than vision-first outlook."

"The gap between ITS and Starship is real, but I would not consider that a failure," he said.

In his view, the rocket is mainly a business tool. "The rocket is the means, not the end," Renčelj said, adding that its main role now is cutting Starlink deployment costs. SpaceX currently operates a constellation of more than 11,000 Starlink broadband satellites, almost all of which were launched by its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket. But Starship Flight 14 lofted the first members of the next-gen Starlink V3 constellation, which will eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft, if all goes to plan. Starlink V3 satellites are bigger and heavier than their predecessors and can only be launched efficiently by Starship.

Renčelj said the moon focus reflects Washington's priorities and SpaceX's interest in staying central to NASA's Artemis program, and in reassuring investors after the company's acquisition of xAI this past February and its IPO, which occurred in June.

Joseph Gonzalez, a University of Illinois Grainger College of Engineering aerospace professor who spent about a decade working on Artemis, sees it differently.

"I think SpaceX is still very much targeting Mars," he said. "SpaceX continues to stress making humanity multiplanetary and establishing a self-sufficient city on Mars as long-term objectives." Gonzalez sees the moon as a proving ground rather than a replacement. Just days away from Earth, the moon lets engineers find problems "before committing humans to a Mars mission."

"Space exploration takes time, especially when you are developing a human spaceflight system with this level of complexity," Gonzalez said. "They build, fly, learn, make changes and fly again. That creates very visible successes and failures, but it also allows engineers to accumulate flight experience and data quickly."

Challenges remain

Reaching Earth orbit isn't the hard part for Starship. Gonzalez said that the most underrated gap is the large-scale cryogenic propellant transfer between vehicles once in orbit. SpaceX has moved propellant between tanks in one Ship before, but its architecture requires numerous transfers involving tanker ships to refill a fuel depot, which a Ship must visit in order to make journeys to the moon or Mars. Gonzalez described this depot as a gas station in space, but there are challenges typical gas stations don't face. The fuel is extremely cold, for example, and it needs to be moved in microgravity conditions.

That milestone is yet to happen, and the timeline for an attempt is not clear. It could potentially come with Flight 15 and 16. These were aspirationally scheduled for no earlier than mid and late October, respectively, but have now apparently slipped to mid-to-late November (though there has been no public confirmation of any firm target date).

In 2025, Musk said there was a "50/50" chance of Starship making a run for Mars in 2026. However, with the once-every-26-months Mars launch window — which lasts a few weeks, opening in late October — and no propellant transfer demonstration yet in the books, that is off the table. The next such low-energy orbital transfer opportunity for the Red Planet opens in late 2028, running into early 2029. At the same time, NASA is currently targeting late 2028 for its Artemis IV mission — which involves Starship — to return humans to the lunar surface after an absence of more than 50 years, giving SpaceX a challenging deadline toward which to work. The company will need to dedicate key resources to meet that timeline, including developing life support systems for crew.

For now, Starship's most immediate role is hauling Starlink satellites in orbit. Renčelj noted that startups raising billions are betting on Starship delivering low super-launch prices along with Falcon 9-like reliability. "Their business models are underpinned by what might be a single point of failure," he said.

"Starship still has major capabilities to demonstrate before it can perform the complete missions envisioned for the moon and Mars," said Gonzalez.

"So I would say the timelines are comparable considering the ambition of the vehicles," he added. "The bigger difference isn't necessarily how many years they have taken, but it's where and how each program chooses to learn during those years."

Musk has repeatedly talked of getting thousands, or even hundreds of thousands, of people on Mars "to make life multiplanetary." Most immediately, SpaceX has a number of business goals and lunar commitments to adhere to ahead of a first uncrewed visit to Mars. Late 2028 appears to be the next real opportunity.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 14, 1947: Test pilot Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier in the Bell X-1, the first X-plane ]]>

On Oct. 14, 1947, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier for the first time!

Chuck Yeager was a test pilot for the U.S. Air Force who made history by flying an aircraft faster than the speed of sound.

Yeager made his historic flight in a Bell X-1 rocket plane that he named "Glamorous Glennis" after his wife. Yeager had broken two ribs the night before when he fell off a horse, but that didn't stop him!

His aircraft was dropped from a Boeing B-29 bomber before accelerating to a speed of Mach 1.07, which is about 821 mph (1,321 km/h). The speed of sound, Mach 1, is about 760 mph (1,223 km/h).

Why it mattered

Before Yeager made his daring Bell X-1 flight, piloted supersonic flight was only a concept.

The Bell X-1 began its life as the XS-1, a cooperative project between NASA's predecessor the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) and the U.S. Army Forces, which would evolve later into the U.S. Air Force. Bell Aircraft won the contract to build the experimental plane in March 1945 and was delivered in December of that year.

The final vehicle was a single-piloted aircraft that was just over 30 feet (nearly 11 meters) long, had a wingspan of about 28 feet (8.5 m) and powered by a rocket engine using liquid oxygen and ethyl alcohol in water as propellant. Yeager's historic flight followed a series of unpowered glide tests, incuding three by Yeager himself in August of 1947, followed by ever faster subsonic powered flights.

"The first generation X-1 aircraft changed aviation history in numerous ways, and not simply because they were the first aircraft to fly faster than the speed of sound," NASA wrote in an overview. "Rather, they established the concept of the research aircraft, built solely for experimental purposes, and unhampered by any military or commercial requirements."

According to NASA, Yeager's history-making flight wasn't immediately known to the public, a departure from the agency's X-plane tests today.

"Yeager reached a speed of Mach 1.06 at 43,000 feet, becoming the first man to fly supersonic. Air Force officials designated the flight and all data as Top Secret two hours later," NASA wrote. "Not until December 1947 would word leak of the achievement, and it was not until March 1948 that the U.S. Air Force officially confirmed the achievement."

Yeager's flight and the X-1 program laid the foundation for an ever-more-ambitious X-plane program that continues at NASA and in the U.S. military today.

NASA's latest X-plane is the X-59 supersonic plane, which is designed to test supersonic flight with quieter sonic booms as way to open up supersonic travel over land for wider commercial use.

]]> <![CDATA[ Life after the moon: Artemis II's Christina Koch steps down from active astronaut duty ]]> Don't expect any of the Artemis II moon astronauts to fly again soon.

On Tuesday (Oct. 13), NASA announced that Artemis II mission specialist Christina Koch will become the agency’s acting deputy chief engineer, effective Nov. 1.

"With this appointment, Koch will transition to management astronaut status and will no longer be eligible for future spaceflight assignments," NASA officials wrote in a statement on Tuesday.

Her three Artemis II crewmates had already shared their next moves, none of which put another spaceflight in play in the near future.

Mission commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover, both of NASA, became "emeritus" astronauts last month, a role that seems to include planning, advising and mentoring duties but no flights into the final frontier. Glover will also work full-time at his alma mater, the California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly) in San Luis Obispo.

"I'm grateful they will continue sharing what they learned with our astronauts, flight controllers and engineers as we prepare for Artemis III in 2027 and the missions that follow," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said of Wiseman and Glover in a Sept. 9 statement.

The fourth Artemis II astronaut, mission specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency, announced a change of his own in July: He planned to become a reservist in the Royal Canadian Air Force, where he's also a colonel. That move became official last month as well.

Artemis II sent the four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon in an Orion capsule. It was the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program and the first human spaceflight beyond low Earth orbit (LEO) since Apollo 17 in 1972.

As Isaacman mentioned, the next mission in the program is Artemis III, a docking test in LEO scheduled to launch next year. The Artemis III crew, which was announced in June, consists of NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik (commander), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio (mission specialists) and Luca Parmitano of the European Space Agency (pilot).

If all goes according to plan, Artemis IV will land astronauts near the moon's south pole in 2028. We don't yet know who will fly on that historic mission.

Koch will succeed current NASA Deputy Chief Engineer Katherine Van Hooser, who will retire on Oct. 21 after more than 35 years of work for the space agency.

"In her new role, Koch will help lead NASA's engineering community, supporting technical oversight, mission readiness, and engineering excellence across the agency's programs and projects," agency officials said in Tuesday's statement.

Koch is a natural choice for the job, given her education and experience. She holds bachelor's degrees in electrical engineering and physics and a master's in electrical engineering, and she began her NASA career as an electrical engineer at Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland.

NASA selected Koch as an astronaut candidate in 2013. She has two spaceflights under her belt: Artemis II and a 328-day-flight to the International Space Station that launched in March 2019. That's the longest space mission ever conducted by a woman, and it featured the first three all-female spacewalks, which Koch conducted with fellow NASA astronaut Jessica Meir.

"Christina has seen NASA engineering from both sides of the equation: developing complex systems on the ground and trusting them with her life in space," Isaacman said in the Tuesday statement.

"After spending nearly a year living and working aboard the International Space Station and helping lead America back around the moon on Artemis II this year, she brings an extraordinary combination of technical expertise, operational experience, and judgment to this role," he added. "I am excited to see the impact she will have across NASA as we return Americans to the lunar surface, build the Moon Base, get underway on nuclear power in space, and develop the capabilities that will ultimately take us on to Mars."

  <item>
   <title>XFG není nová varianta covidu, říká viroložka. Příznaky má ale specifické</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/zdravotnictvi/zdravi-covid-xfg-priznaky-chrapot-paleni-v-krku-kasel/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zdravotnictvi</link>
   <description>Subvarianta covidu XFG, známá jako Stratus, nyní dominuje v Evropě i u nás. Ačkoli ji někteří označují za novou či americkou mutaci, virologové upozorňují, že cirkuluje již od minulého roku. Současné vakcíny ji obsahují jako vakcinační kmen. Odborníci doporučují očkování rizikovým skupinám, přičemž zdůrazňují vhodné načasování vzhledem k nadcházející chřipkové sezóně. Hlavními příznaky jsou pálení v krku, chrapot a kašel. Deník.cz přináší přehled nejčastejších otázek spojených s covidem XFG.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:51:36 +0200</pubDate>

   <title>Babí léto se vrátí, tvrdí meteorologové. Ještě předtím ale přijde teplotní šok</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/predpoved-pocasi-cesko-okraje-babi-leto-nekonci-prijde-ale-ochlazeni-zlom-radar/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Konec pracovního týdne přinese změnu charakteru počasí. Zatímco v pátek mohou teploty někde atakovat i „dvacítku“, o víkendu se citelně ochladí a teplotní rozdíl může být i deset stupňů Celsia. Kromě toho přibude oblačnost a místy se objeví slabé přeháňky. Teplým a slunečným dnům ale rozhodně není konec a do Česka se po víkendové přestávce vrátí babí léto. Sucho se tak bude nadále prohlubovat.</description>

  <item>
   <title>U zámku v Zákupech začala obnova další části hospodářského dvora za 242 milionů</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/u-zamku-v-zakupech-zacala-obnova-dalsi-casti-hospodarskeho-dvora-za-242-milionu/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>U státního zámku v Zákupech předáním staveniště začala obnova další části hospodářského dvora z konce 17. století, který je národní kulturní památkou. Stát bude 242 milionů korun a práce potrvají do roku 2029. Obnovené prostory budou sloužit jako zázemí zámku a do doby zřízení depozitáře také pro uložení archeologických nálezů.   </description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 12:04:57 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/u-zamku-v-zakupech-zacala-obnova-dalsi-casti-hospodarskeho-dvora-za-242-milionu/</guid>
   <category>Českolipsko </category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/f9f/f9fa1089-3db2-414d-9b7f-40080e0d0298.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/f9f/f9fa1089-3db2-414d-9b7f-40080e0d0298.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Hospodářský dvůr zámku v Zákupech, kde začala obnova jižní části a západního křídla, ve kterém byl v minulosti pivovar. </media:description>
    <media:credit>Petra Hámová</media:credit>
   </media:content>

  <item>
   <title>Platit si jídlo a pobyt v domově důchodců ze svého? Návrh vyvolal smršť reakcí</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/ekonomika-domovy-duchodcu-navrh-platit-si-jidlo-ubytovani-/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Jídlo a ubytování v domovech seniorů a obdobných zařízeních za své, případně s pomocí rodiny? Návrh Asociace poskytovatelů sociálních služeb ČR, o kterém Deník.cz nedávno informoval a k němuž se ministerští úředníci staví rezervovaně, vyvolal mezi čtenáři zájem i polemiky. Přinášíme proto další informace včetně názorů lidí z oboru. Shodují se na tom, že systém musí mít jasná pravidla a o péči nesmí přijít chudší senioři.</description>

   <description>Od 3. října se na českých sociálních sítích šíří falešný snímek zdánlivé titulní stránky periodika, označovaného jako České noviny, s hlavním článkem informujícím o tom, že policie údajně odhalila rozsáhlou síť převážející na české území ukradené spotřebiče z Ukrajiny.   <item>
   <title>Důchody se opět změní. Zohlední péči o děti, vyšší penze čeká na manžele</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-ekonomika-duchody-zmena-2027-zohledneni-pece-o-deti-sdilny-vymerovaci-zaklad-manzelu/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>V příštím roce dozraje čas pro poslední fázi reformních kroků zavedených minulou vládou. Důchody více ocení péči o děti a osoby blízké, zejména ženám by měl také k vyšší penzi pomoci sdílený vyměřovací základ pro manžele. Naopak zatím na obzoru ještě není opětovné zastropování důchodového věku ani úprava valorizačního vzorce, což slibovala současná vláda.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 05:30:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/cesko-ekonomika-duchody-zmena-2027-zohledneni-pece-o-deti-sdilny-vymerovaci-zaklad-manzelu/</guid>

  <item>
   <title>Maturita ve čtyřiceti a hospoda jako koníček. Ano, šéfe! míří do Jenčic</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/kultura/ano-sefe-zdenek-pohlreich-hospudka-u-kastanu-jencice-litomericko/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=kultura</link>
   <description>Zdeněk Kotulán se sedmnáct let živí jako pojišťovací poradce, jeho snem ale vždycky bylo mít vlastní hospodu. Tu si nakonec otevřel v Jenčicích na Litoměřicku. Jenže hosté příliš nechodí a restaurace ho neuživí. Zdeněk Pohlreich tak bude muset poradit nejen s vařením, ale i s tím, jak podnik vůbec udržet při životě. A během natáčení stihne ještě jednu neobvyklou událost: majitelovu maturitu.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 04:30:00 +0200</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Druhé kolo voleb do Senátu: kdy a kde se volí, koho vybrat a jak sehnat hlasovací lístky</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/druhe-kolo-voleb-do-senatu-kdy-a-kde-se-voli-koho-vybrat-a-jak-sehnat-hlasovaci-listky.A261011_110515_volby_wall#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ze sčítání hlasovacích lístků prvního kola senátních voleb ve 27 obvodech vzešlo pět kandidátů, kteří rovnou zamíří do lavic v Senátu. O obsazení mandátů ve zbývajících 22 obvodech voliči rozhodnou ve druhém kole, které se uskuteční v pátek 16. a v sobotu 17. října 2026. Průběh hlasování je stejný, jen na lístky ve schránce budou voliči čekat marně.
</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:18:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/volby">Zprávy - Volby</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/druhe-kolo-voleb-do-senatu-kdy-a-kde-se-voli-koho-vybrat-a-jak-sehnat-hlasovaci-listky.A261011_110515_volby_wall/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261011_110515_volby_wall</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/23/012/cl6/LUH98be1e_12.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Druhé kolo voleb do Senátu proběhne v pátek 16. a v sobotu 17. října 2026.</media:description>
      <media:credit>MAFRA</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>V Rusku zadrželi šéfredaktora nezávislého listu Novaja gazeta</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/sefredaktor-nezavisleho-ruskeho-listu-novaja-gazeta-byl-odvezen-k-vyslechu.A261015_154636_zahranicni_jhr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Sergej Sokolov, šéfredaktor nezávislého listu Novaja gazeta, byl po domovní prohlídce zadržen a odvezen k výslechu. List, který je ruskými úřady označován za takzvaného zahraničního agenta, o tom informoval na platformě Telegram. Za Sokolovem již vyrazil právník. Ruský vyšetřovací výbor, obdoba amerického Federálního úřadu pro vyšetřování (FBI), Sokolova vyslýchá v případu nezákonného použití osobních údajů.</description>
      <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:04:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni">Zprávy - Zahraničí</category>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/102/cl6/JHR85c5c42f8a_profimedia_1143580470.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Sergej Sokolov, šéfredaktor nezávislého ruského listu Novaja gazeta (6. května 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>Profimedia.cz</media:credit>

    <item>
      <title>Neprší a pršet ani nebude, ukázali meteorologové mapu srážek na říjen</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/neprsi-a-prset-ani-nebude-ukazali-meteorologove-mapu-srazek-na-rijen.A261015_124801_domaci_wall#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Podzimní období si většina lidí spojí se sychravým počasím, ranními mlhami, ale hlavně častými dešti a mrholením. Letošní podzim je však podle meteorologů na míle vzdálený zažitým představám. Podle map s předpovědí pro Evropu spadne v Česku jen pár milimetrů srážek. Meteorologové varují, že se ještě prohloubí sucho, se kterým se krajina potýká.</description>

    <item>
      <title>RECENZE: Nejen trčící náhrobky z Lipna. Vltavice odhaluje skrytou paměť místa</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/kultura/literatura/vltavice-jan-stifter-recenze.A261014_123108_literatura_ts#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Nový román jihočeského spisovatele Jana Štiftera (1984) není ani tolik příběh, dějové vyprávění, jako spíš rozsáhlé plátno, kterým prosvítají starší vrstvy. Ovšem plátno monumentální, intenzivní, s jednotlivými detaily propracovanými a propojenými tak, že fungují skvěle ve prospěch finále, a tedy celku.</description>

      <media:description>Sucho odhalilo náhrobky původních obyvatel Dolní Vltavice u lipenské přehrady.</media:description>
      <media:credit>Klára Sváčková, Museum Fotoateliér Seidel</media:credit>
      <media:group>

    <item>
      <title>Antimonopolní úřad: Tendr Českých drah na nákup elektrických vlaků byl v pořádku</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/doprava/uohs-ceske-drahy-tendr-vlak-stadler.A261015_154140_eko-doprava_dvou#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Tendr Českých drah na nákup 133 elektrických vlaků typu EMU 400 pro regionální dopravu byl v pořádku, rozhodl Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže (ÚOHS). Zakázkou se zabýval na podnět skupiny Stadler. Proti rozhodnutí je možné podat rozklad, není zatím pravomocné. Proto nadále platí zákaz uzavřít s vybraným dodavatelem smlouvu.</description>

      <description>Ve Zlíně je blíž nová koalice bez hnutí ANO, které vyhrálo volby.       <title>Zlatá hodinka je tu, zbohatnete. Podvodníci muže obrali o devět milionů</title>

      <description>Příbramští kriminalisté zadrželi kurýra zapojeného do investičního podvodu, při kterém třiašedesátiletý muž přišel o více než devět milionů korun. Policisté kurýra dopadli přímo při přebírání dalších peněz od poškozeného. Cizince soud uznal vinným z legalizace výnosů z trestné činnosti z nedbalosti a na pět let ho vyhostil z Česka.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/ondrej-vlcek-znovu-oficialne-ve-svetove-kyberneticke-lize-startup-aisle-bude-kupovat-kanadska-firma/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Pražský kyberbezpečnostní startup Aisle, za nímž stojí Ondřej Vlček, Stanislav Fort a Jaya Ballo, hodlá koupit kanadská AI společnost Cohere. Praha má být evropskou základnou firmy. Firmy oznámily, že podepsaly předběžnou dohodu o akvizici. Aisle oznámil svou existenci oficiálně teprve loni, po roce práce v utajení, a přitáhl také rovnou renomované investory. Firma vyvíjí umělou inteligenci, která hledá bezpečnostní chyby v softwaru, a za svou existenci už stihla odhalit i takové, které přetrvávaly v kódech celosvětově využívaných služeb hned několik desetiletí. Finanční podmínky dohody společnosti nezveřejnily.</description>

 <description>Americký miliardář Elon Musk napsal na své sociální síti X, že za omezením družicové služby Starshield, která poskytuje podporu ukrajinské armádě, může být administrativa Donalda Trumpa. O provozu tohoto systému rozhoduje velení amerických ozbrojených sil. „Musk sice podporuje Starshield pro obranu Ukrajiny, ale odmítá jakoukoli eskalaci a tvrdí, že má dojít k mírovému řešení,“ říká pro Radiožurnál šéfredaktor serveru 365tipu.cz Daniel Dočekal.</description>

 <description>Rakouský soud propustil z vazby Slováka, který čelí obviněním z otravy výživ potravinářské společnosti HiPP, aby ji tak vydíral. Informovala o tom agentura APA. Slovák, který už dříve vinu odmítl, po dobu nadcházejícího procesu nesmí opustit Rakousko.</description>

 <title>Postavit kryt je teď v Polsku snazší než cokoliv jiného, říká starosta města Malbork, kde je staví jako první </title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/postavit-kryt-je-ted-v-polsku-snazsi-nez-cokoliv-jineho-rika-starosta-mesta_2610151356_jar</link>
 <description>Polská vláda schválila dalších skoro 560 miliard korun na civilní obranu. Investice v následujících pěti letech poslouží k výstavbě civilních krytů, k nákupu záchranného a zdravotnického vybavení nebo k vybudování výstražného systému a bezpečné komunikace. Program ochrany obyvatelstva a civilní obrany funguje v Polsku od loňského roku a čerpá z něj například Malbork. Jako první v Polsku nyní buduje moderní protichemické a protiatomové kryty.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Stopka pro Rooneyovou. Kvůli podpoře Palestine Action se v Británii nebudou prodávat její knihy</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/stopka-pro-spisovatelku-rooneyovou-kvuli-podpore-palestincu-se-v-britanii_2610151354_ako</link>
 <description>Ve Velké Británii se přestanou prodávat knihy irské spisovatelky Sally Rooneyové kvůli jejímu záměru použít výnosy pro propalestinskou skupinu Palestine Action, jež Londýn zakázal jako teroristickou organizaci. Autorka i nakladatelství Faber to oznámily ve středu. Ten uvedl, že mu zákony neumožňují předávat Rooneyové příjmy z prodeje knih v Británii, proto se v Británii prodávat nebudou. Jinde budou dostupné, informovaly agentury Reuters a AP.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-14t151142z_1_261015-133442_ako.JPG?itok=OQNusKEn" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Trump a jeho poradci zvažují, jak ukončit válku v Íránu. Mezi možnostmi je i ‚matka všech bomb‘</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/trump-a-jeho-poradci-zvazuji-jak-ukoncit-valku-v-iranu-mezi-moznostmi-je-i-matka_2610151344_raf</link>
 <description>Ozbrojené síly USA vypracovaly nové plány úderů na Írán, které zahrnují možné použití jejich nejsilnější nejaderné bomby GBU-43/B, přezdívané „matka všech bomb“. S odvoláním na informované zdroje to ve čtvrtek napsal web stanice CNN. Plány připravené pro případné rozhodnutí prezidenta Donalda Trumpa obnovit vojenské operace před listopadovými volbami do Kongresu či po nich mezi cíle útoků zařadily jaderná zařízení a energetickou infrastrukturu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2017-04-13t000000z_3_261015-132055_raf.JPG?itok=xtjZig3b" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Loni jsme měli volby, ne revoluci.‘ Albánský premiér odmítl rezignovat navzdory studentským protestům</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/loni-jsme-meli-volby-ne-revoluci-albansky-premier-odmitl-rezignovat-navzdory_2610151239_med</link>
 <description>Albánský premiér Edi Rama odmítl odstoupit z funkce navzdory násilným studentským protestům, které zemí zmítají již třetím dnem. Demonstranti kritizují současnou vládu a stav školství a žádají demisi šéfa vlády. Rama podle agentury Reuters zdůraznil, že nedovolí, aby násilnosti zmařily snahu Albánie o vstup do Evropské unie.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/img_1655_260620-112634_aru.jpeg?itok=dF-irKim" type="image/jpeg" />

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ukrajina-zasahla-sest-ruskych-bombarderu-ve-voronezske-oblasti-oznamil_2610151142_ako</link>
 <description>Ukrajina v noci na čtvrtek zaútočila na vojenské letiště Borisoglebsk v ruské Voroněžské oblasti a zasáhla šest bombardérů Suchoj Su-34M, oznámilo na facebooku ukrajinské námořnictvo. Zároveň uvedlo, že útočilo raketovým komplexem Neptun. Moskva se k těmto informacím nevyjádřila.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-107023779_261015-110443_ako.jpg?itok=f3D8AdUk" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Po zřícení střechy školy v Pákistánu zahynulo 32 dětí a učitel. Zranění utrpěly na tři desítky lidí </title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/nejmene-17-deti-a-ucitel-zahynuli-po-zriceni-strechy-skoly-v-pakistanu-nekteri_2610150927_med</link>
 <description>Nejméně 32 žáků, většinou mladších 13 let, a jeden učitel přišli ve čtvrtek o život, když se během výuky zřítila střecha školy v Péšávaru na severozápadě Pákistánu. Informovaly o tom tiskové agentury s odvoláním na mluvčího nemocnice. Zraněno bylo dalších asi 30 lidí, z toho šest bylo hospitalizováno v kritickém stavu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-15t075949z_2_261015-131713_ako.JPG?itok=Zh9h9BsE" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:27:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Ukrajina začne opět útočit na ruské rafinerie. Spory s USA pomáhají Putinovi, řekl Zelenskyj</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ukrajina-zacne-opet-utocit-na-ruske-rafinerie-spory-s-usa-pomahaji_2610150745_dns</link>
 <description>Ukrajina začne zase útočit na rafinerie v Rusku, řekl v rozhovoru, který ve čtvrtek ráno zveřejnil deník Financial Times, ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj. Ukrajina tyto údery na několik dnů přerušila kvůli energetickému příměří, které v neděli ohlásil americký prezident Donald Trump. Kyjev ale poukazoval, že Rusko i nadále útočilo na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-07-01t133704z_2_260717-110318_ako.JPG?itok=_T2mxd0h" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 07:45:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Britská vláda finančně pomůže s opravou sarkofágu v Černobylu. Minulý únor ho zasáhl dron</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/britska-vlada-financne-pomuze-s-opravou-sarkofagu-v-cernobylu-minuly-unor-ho_2610150735_raf</link>
 <description>Británie poskytne 17 milionů liber (490 milionů korun) na opravu sarkofágu jaderné elektrárny v Černobylu, který poničil v loňském roce útok. Uvedla to ve čtvrtek britská vláda. Ukrajina a Británie přisuzují útok dronu, který poškodil ochranný štít elektrárny, Rusku. Moskva to ale odmítla s tvrzením, že neútočí na jadernou infrastrukturu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-096375793_250214-144109_adn.jpg?itok=pK9c9zD5" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>V Liberci vyrostlo největší solární parkoviště v Česku. Je v areálu DENSO</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903139-v-liberci-vyrostlo-nejvetsi-solarni-parkoviste-v-cesku-je-v-arealu-denso.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903139-v-liberci-vyrostlo-nejvetsi-solarni-parkoviste-v-cesku-je-v-arealu-denso.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Největší solární parkoviště v ČR vyrostlo v areálu DENSO v průmyslové zóně v Liberci. Takzvaný carport tvoří 2 706 solárních panelů, jejich výkon bude 1,8 MWp, zaparkovat pod nimi může 482 aut. Firma tak využila parkoviště k výrobě zelené energie, zároveň zlepšila komfort parkování pro zaměstnance.</description></item><item><title>Arsenal má náhradu za odvolaného Mathausera. Přichází Chorvat Matić</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903138-arsenal-ma-nahradu-za-odvolaneho-mathausera-prichazi-chorvat-mati.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903138-arsenal-ma-nahradu-za-odvolaneho-mathausera-prichazi-chorvat-mati.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:42:09 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Českolipský Arsenal představil trenéra, který nahradí odvolaného Petra Mathausera. Do Česka přichází zcela nové trenérské jméno – sedmačtyřicetiletý Chorvat Stipe Matić. Ten má trenérské zkušenosti ze švýcarského Thunu. Naposledy pracoval jako skaut.</description></item><item><title>Zajímavost voleb. Hned několik obcí s lyžařskými středisky čeká výměna starosty</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903077-krkonosskou-rokytnici-benecko-vitkovice-a-asi-i-harrachov-ceka-vymena.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903077-krkonosskou-rokytnici-benecko-vitkovice-a-asi-i-harrachov-ceka-vymena.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nového starostu bude mít většina obcí se známými lyžařskými areály v Libereckém kraji. Jiného budou mít krkonošská střediska Rokytnice nad Jizerou, Benecko, Vítkovice a nejspíš i Harrachov. V jizerskohorském Bedřichově možná zůstane stávající, povolební vyjednávání tam ale ještě neskončila.</description></item><item><title>Změna na průtahu. Směr na Prahu se uzavře, k OC Nisa a na Dlouhý most nesjedete</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903085-zmena-na-prutahu-smer-na-prahu-se-uzavre-k-oc-nisa-a-na-dlouhy-most-nesjedete.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903085-zmena-na-prutahu-smer-na-prahu-se-uzavre-k-oc-nisa-a-na-dlouhy-most-nesjedete.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:57:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Už v sobotu dojde k další změně v omezení na průtahu Libercem. Půjde o opravovaný úsek mezi Makrem a sjezdem u benzínové čerpací stanice Čermák. Zavřený bude jízdní pás ve směru z Děčína na Prahu a doprava opět povede v protisměrném jízdním pásu v režimu 1+1.</description></item><item><title>Technické služby Liberce vybudují tři vrty, ušetří za pitnou vodu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903067-technicke-sluzby-liberce-vybuduji-tri-vrty-usetri-za-pitnou-vodu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903067-technicke-sluzby-liberce-vybuduji-tri-vrty-usetri-za-pitnou-vodu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Městské technické služby Liberce (TSML) vybudují tři vrty ve svém areálu v Otavské ulici. Ušetří díky nim za pitnou vodu, navíc budou mít jistotu zdroje, pokud by nastalo sucho a nemohly odebírat povrchovou vodu. Vybudování vrtů si vyžádá zhruba tři miliony korun.</description></item><item><title>Liberečtí policisté stopli milionový podvod. Falešný kurýr dojezdil</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903069-liberecti-policiste-stopli-milionovy-podvod-falesny-kuryr-dojezdil.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903069-liberecti-policiste-stopli-milionovy-podvod-falesny-kuryr-dojezdil.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:51:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Liberečtí kriminalisté dopadli třiadvacetiletého cizince, který jako kurýr přebíral peníze od oběti investičního podvodu. Žena muži postupně předala přes dva miliony korun. Při čtvrtém pokusu kontaktovala policii, která podvodníka zadržela přímo při předání. Nyní mu hrozí až pět let vězení.</description></item><item><title>Ve Frýdlantu je už po volbách jasno. Kdo bude starostou, místostarostou a v radě?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903065-ve-frydlantu-je-uz-po-volbach-jasno-kdo-bude-starostou-mistostarostou-a-v-rade.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903065-ve-frydlantu-je-uz-po-volbach-jasno-kdo-bude-starostou-mistostarostou-a-v-rade.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Povolební jednání ve Frýdlantu významně postoupila. Zástupci tří volebních uskupení: Frýdlantu pro všechny, Místních a SLK a Nezávislých pro Frýdlant uzavřeli ve středu večer koaliční dohodu. Starostou se podle ní má stát dosavadní místostarosta Jiří Stodůlka, místostarostou nováček Martin Roušal.</description></item><item><title>Tygři vyhráli v Davosu a v Lize mistrů si zahrají vyřazovací část</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/903058-tygri-vyhrali-v-davosu-a-v-lize-mistru-si-zahraji-vyrazovaci-cast.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/903058-tygri-vyhrali-v-davosu-a-v-lize-mistru-si-zahraji-vyrazovaci-cast.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Oct 2026 22:04:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Liberečtí hokejisté se v posledním utkání základní části Ligy mistrů představili na ledě švýcarského Davosu. Pro postup do vyřazovací části jim stačilo získat bod a nakonec mají rovnou tři. Po brankách Vlacha a Galvase vyhráli 2:0.</description></item><item><title>KOMENTÁŘ: Kdo zaplatí účet za Babišovu nevýhru?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/blogy-a-komentare/902959-komentar-kdo-zaplati-ucet-za-babisovu-nevyhru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/blogy-a-komentare/902959-komentar-kdo-zaplati-ucet-za-babisovu-nevyhru.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Oct 2026 20:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Antonín Berdych</dc:creator><category>Blogy a komentáře</category><description>Při hodnocení komunálních voleb je třeba připomenout, s jakou výchozí pozicí do nich strany vstupovaly. ANO v průzkumech překračovalo třicet procent, součet opozičních stran byl však vyšší.</description></item><item><title>Osudná chyba při vloupání v Pražské ulici. Zloději zapomněli na věc, která je usvědčila</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/902995-straznici-v-liberci-zadrzeli-v-parku-v-zeyerove-ulici-tri-podezrele-z-vloupani-do-prodejny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/902995-straznici-v-liberci-zadrzeli-v-parku-v-zeyerove-ulici-tri-podezrele-z-vloupani-do-prodejny.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Oct 2026 18:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Strážníci v Liberci zadrželi v parku v Zeyerově ulici tři podezřelé z vloupání do prodejny v centru města v Pražské. Pachatele zachytil městský kamerový systém, díky jeho záznamům získala hlídka přesný popis. Po krátkém výslechu na místě byli všichni omezeni na osobní svobodě a předáni policii ČR.</description></item></channel></rss>
